name: CMS: WP users -> xmlrpc surface -> debug log -> credentials
goal: Chain WordPress recon skills into a credentials story: enumerate users, map xmlrpc methods, recover leaked logs.
impact: User list, xmlrpc brute surface, log-recovered secrets — feeds auth chains.

steps.purpose: REST users endpoint leaks the author/admin namespace.
steps.on_fail: REST blocked -> sitemap author archives, ?author=N redirects (documented variants).

steps.purpose: xmlrpc exposes system.listMethods + wp.getUsersBlogs — the brute surface.
steps.on_success: xmlrpc available -> password brute is the documented follow-up (needs burst tooling).
steps.on_fail: xmlrpc disabled -> REST auth attempts with username list.

steps.purpose: wp-content/debug.log leaks errors incl. paths, SQL fragments, plugin internals.
steps.on_success: Log-derived secrets/paths -> targeted attacks; also proves poor ops hygiene for the report.
steps.on_fail: No log -> other secrets_exposure artifacts (.env/backup) on the same host.

recon.name: Plugin/version census
recon.how: readme.txt and ?v= style versions map plugin CVEs (per-product — extend on demand).

recon.name: Author archive pivots
recon.how: ?author=N and sitemap author lists when REST users is blocked.

recon.name: Config-artifact pairing
recon.how: wp-config backups, .env files, and SQL dump artifacts (secrets_exposure shelf) recover DB creds and salts that pair with the user list.
recon.signal: Credentials or table prefixes from artifacts.

variants: theme editor abuse when admin reached
pivot_hints: admin reach -> theme editor = SSTI/RCE-like impact (documented variant)
